rows.name: API_KEY
rows.values: Any text. The script does not check it.
rows.default: Unset: the script sends the text `YOUR_API_KEY`. An empty value counts as unset.
rows.effect: `burst-test.sh` (the script that sends a burst of chat completion requests to a server) puts the value in the header `Authorization: Bearer <value>` of every request.
rows.notes: The option `-k` or `--key` overrides the variable.

rows.name: API_URL
rows.values: URL of a chat completions endpoint. `curl` receives the text unchanged.
rows.default: Unset: `http://localhost:3000/v1/chat/completions`. An empty value counts as unset.
rows.effect: `burst-test.sh` (the script that sends a burst of chat completion requests to a server) posts every request to this URL with `curl`.
rows.notes: The option `-u` or `--url` overrides the variable.

evidence.quote: # POST JSON body $1 to API_URL, passing any extra curl options in $2...

rows.name: CABAL_FLAGS
rows.values: Extra options for `cabal run`, separated by white space. The script splits the text with `str.split()`. Quote characters do not group words.
rows.default: Unset: no extra option. An empty value behaves the same.
rows.effect: `build-model.py` (the ingest script for one model) inserts the options between `cabal run` and `ingest` in the command that translates the exported trace into plugin code. `cabal` is the Haskell build tool.
rows.notes: Read only when neither `--ingest-bin` nor `--export-only` is given. `make build-all-coverage` in `ingest/` sets the coverage build options. `ingest/Makefile` assigns its own make variable `CABAL_FLAGS` empty. A value from the environment does not reach its `cabal test` commands.

rows.name: COVERAGE
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns coverage mode on. The script does not parse the text. The value `0` also turns it on.
rows.default: Unset: coverage mode is off. An empty value counts as unset.
rows.effect: `build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for every model of the model registry) handles only the models that `RUN_COVERAGE` lists. It sets `HPCTIXFILE` per model, and each run writes its own `.tix` file (Haskell coverage counts). At the end it combines the files.
rows.notes: The script adds no coverage option to the `cabal` command. `make build-all-coverage` in `ingest/` sets `COVERAGE=1` and passes the coverage options in `CABAL_FLAGS`. The CMake option `COVERAGE` is a different setting. It is not an environment variable.

rows.name: COVERAGE_BASELINE
rows.who_sets: CI workflow `ingest-coverage.yml` sets `35`. Developers set it locally.
rows.values: Whole number of percent, for example `35`. The recipe does not check the text. With text that is not an integer, the comparison fails and the recipe prints `PASS`.
rows.default: Unset: the recipe stops with a shell error that contains `COVERAGE_BASELINE not set`. An empty value behaves the same.
rows.effect: It is the lowest accepted expression coverage of the ingest Haskell code, in percent. The recipe rounds the measured coverage to the nearest 5 percent. The target fails when the rounded value is below the baseline.
rows.notes: The CI workflow sets `35`. It also reports the rounded coverage minus the baseline. `coverage-check` reads the summary of the test coverage. `coverage-check-combined` reads the combined summary.

rows.name: COVERAGE_TIX_DIR
rows.values: Path of a directory. A relative path is relative to the working directory of the script.
rows.default: Unset: `dist-newstyle/coverage/build-all-tix`. An empty value counts as unset.
rows.effect: In coverage mode `build-all.sh` creates the directory. It writes one `.tix` file (Haskell coverage counts) per model there. Then it combines all `.tix` files of the directory into `build-all-combined.tix`.
rows.notes: Used only when `COVERAGE` is not empty. `.tix` files of an earlier run are combined too. `make build-all-coverage` deletes them first. `make coverage-combine` reads only `dist-newstyle/coverage/build-all-tix/build-all-combined.tix`.

rows.name: CPUAFFINITY
rows.who_sets: An environment file of the unit. This repository does not set it.
rows.values: A CPU list in the form that `taskset -c` accepts. TRON code does not parse it.
rows.default: Unset: the unit and the drop-in give no fallback value. No file in this repository sets the variable.
rows.effect: The unit starts rinzler with `/usr/bin/taskset -c <value>`. The list is the set of CPUs that the rinzler process may run on. The `tron-host` drop-in starts `rinzler_host` (the rinzler build for CPU inference) the same way.
rows.notes: The unit loads two environment files: `/etc/rinzler/instance-<id>.env` and the optional `/opt/positron/user/config.env`. A unit comment says that platformd writes the first file. The unit sets `SyslogIdentifier=rinzler`. The journal then shows `rinzler`, not `taskset`.

rows.name: DUMP_ALL
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The script does not parse the text. The value `0` also turns it on.
rows.default: Unset: off. An empty value counts as unset.
rows.effect: `build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for every model of the model registry) adds `--dump-all` to every `build-model.py` call. `build-model.py` then passes `--dump-all` and `--dump-name <model name>` to the ingest program.
rows.notes: The help text of `--dump-all` is "Enable dump output from ingest". No effect when `EXPORT_ONLY` is set. `build-model.py` then returns before it starts the ingest program.

rows.name: EXPORT_ARGS
rows.values: Extra command-line arguments for `build-model.py`. The shell splits the text at white space and expands wildcard characters. Quote characters do not group words.
rows.default: Unset: no extra argument. An empty value behaves the same.
rows.effect: `build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for every model of the model registry) adds the words to the arguments of every `build-model.py` call.
rows.notes: The script puts its own arguments after these words, for example `--meta-device`, `--target-executor` and `--moe-router`.

rows.name: EXPORT_DIR
rows.values: Path of a directory. A relative path is relative to the working directory of the script.
rows.default: Unset: `exports`. An empty value counts as unset.
rows.effect: `build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for every model of the model registry) creates the directory. For each model it passes `<EXPORT_DIR>/<model>` as `--trace-dir` to `build-model.py`. It writes the log to `<EXPORT_DIR>/<model>.log`.
rows.notes: Each `/` in the model ID becomes `-` in these two names.

rows.name: EXPORT_ONLY
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The script does not parse the text. The value `0` also turns it on.
rows.default: Unset: off. An empty value counts as unset.
rows.effect: `build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for every model of the model registry) adds `--export-only` to every `build-model.py` call. `build-model.py` then exports the trace and stops. It does not start the ingest program and does not update the config file.

evidence.quote: help="Only export trace, skip ingest and config update",

rows.name: GHC
rows.who_sets: The Nix dev shell sets `ghc`. CMake sets it for child commands.
rows.values: Name or full path of the GHC program (the Haskell compiler). CMake does not accept a directory.
rows.default: Unset: CMake searches only for `ghc-9.12` and `ghc`, plus `ghc-9.12.2` when `IN_NIX_SHELL` is not defined. `build-model.py` uses `ghc`. Empty: `build-model.py` passes an empty `-w` value.
rows.effect: The two readers differ. CMake uses the value as the last candidate name in its search for the compiler, after its fixed names. `build-model.py` passes the value to `cabal run` as the compiler option `-w`.
rows.notes: A fixed name that CMake finds wins over the value. CMake stores the found path in the cache variable `GHC_EXECUTABLE` and then does not search again. Without `IN_NIX_SHELL` the found compiler must report version 9.12.2. `build-model.py` reads `GHC` only without `--ingest-bin` and `--export-only`.

rows.name: HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN
rows.who_sets: A developer who runs the tree-vis scripts.
rows.values: A Hugging Face access token. Any non-empty text is used unchanged.
rows.default: Unset: the scripts pass no token, unless an earlier source gives one. An empty value behaves the same.
rows.effect: The tree-vis scripts (they draw token trees for the KV cache documentation) pass the token to `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained` when they load a tokenizer.
rows.notes: It is the last source. `gen.py` first uses `tokenizer.hf_token` of its YAML input, then `HF_TOKEN`. `tokenizer.py` first uses `--hf-token`, then `HF_TOKEN`. No other file in TRON reads this name.

evidence.quote: hf_token = args.hf_token or os.getenv("HF_TOKEN") or os.getenv("HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN")

rows.name: MAX_TOKENS_BASE
rows.values: Whole number of tokens from `1` to `999999999`, without a leading zero. It must be larger than `MAX_TOKENS_JITTER`. Any other value stops the script with exit status 1.
rows.default: Unset: 512 tokens. An empty value counts as unset.
rows.effect: It is the middle of the `max_tokens` range of `burst-test.sh` (the script that sends a burst of chat completion requests to a server). Each request gets a random `max_tokens` from base minus jitter to base plus jitter.
rows.notes: The option `-t` or `--max-tokens` overrides the variable. The script header says that long prompt mode needs a server context window of `PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX` plus base plus jitter tokens.

evidence.quote: echo "$var must be a non-negative integer, got '${!var}'" >&2

rows.name: MAX_TOKENS_JITTER
rows.values: Whole number of tokens from `0`, at most 9 digits, no leading zero. It must be smaller than `MAX_TOKENS_BASE`. Any other value stops the script with exit status 1.
rows.default: Unset: 128 tokens. An empty value counts as unset.
rows.effect: It is half of the width of the random `max_tokens` range of `burst-test.sh` (the script that sends a burst of chat completion requests to a server). Each request gets a `max_tokens` from base minus jitter to base plus jitter. The value `0` gives every request the base value.
rows.notes: The option `-j` or `--jitter` overrides the variable.

evidence.quote: echo "$var must be a non-negative integer, got '${!var}'" >&2

rows.name: MODEL
rows.values: A model name as text. The script does not check it.
rows.default: Unset: `llama-3.2-3b-instruct-fast-tp2`. An empty value counts as unset.
rows.effect: `burst-test.sh` (the script that sends a burst of chat completion requests to a server) puts the value in the `model` field of every request.
rows.notes: The option `-m` or `--model` overrides the variable.

rows.name: NO_META
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The script does not parse the text. The value `0` also turns it on.
rows.default: Unset: `build-all.sh` adds `--meta-device` to every `build-model.py` call. An empty value counts as unset.
rows.effect: `build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for every model of the model registry) leaves out `--meta-device`. The export step then builds each model with zero-filled weights in CPU memory. With `--meta-device` the parameters stay on the PyTorch meta device (tensors with a shape and no data).
rows.notes: The help text of `--meta-device` is "Use meta device for zero memory footprint (experimental)".

new_terms.definition: The script `perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh`. It sends a burst of chat completion requests to a server while a Perfetto capture runs.
The script `ingest/build-all.sh`. It runs `build-model.py` for every model that the model registry lists for ingest.
The script `ingest/build-model.py`. It exports the trace of one model and starts the ingest program that translates the trace into plugin code.
The file `config/models.yaml`. It lists the models that TRON knows.
The PyTorch export of one model. The ingest program reads it.
The Haskell executable `ingest`. It translates a trace into the C++ plugin code of a model.
A file with the coverage counts of one run of a Haskell program that is built with coverage.
A PyTorch device. Its tensors have a shape and no data.
The rinzler build for CPU inference. The `tron-host` package installs it for test and development hosts.
The scripts under `doc/tree-vis`. They draw token trees for the KV cache documentation.
The Linux command that starts a program on a given list of CPUs.

notes: All 17 rows are kept. Source code was opened for every variable. CPUAFFINITY is not a developer tool variable: systemd expands it in the packaged unit `rinzler@.service`, so a deployment section fits it better than tools. CPUAFFINITY: the behaviour for an unset value depends on systemd and taskset, which are not in the checkout, so the row states only that no fallback exists. GHC: the comment at flake.nix:1876 says the variable prevents the use of ghcup. The code does not do that: `ENV GHC` stands inside the NAMES list of find_program, the fixed names are tried first, and `$HOME/.ghcup/bin` stays in the search path. Three facts rest on tool behaviour that was checked with scratch input outside the checkout (no file written): (1) CMake 3.22.1 treats `ENV GHC` inside NAMES as one more candidate name after the listed names; a full path and a bare name work, a directory does not. (2) GNU Make 4.3: the assignment `CABAL_FLAGS :=` in ingest/Makefile hides a value from the caller's environment, and recipes see an empty value. (3) dash and bash: `[ 35 -lt abc ]` reports an error and the `if` takes the else branch, so a non-integer COVERAGE_BASELINE prints PASS. config/test_model_definitions.py sets COVERAGE and EXPORT_ARGS to empty and EXPORT_DIR to a temporary directory for its own run of build-all.sh; the rows do not mention this test. Evidence quotes are the source lines without leading and trailing white space; Makefile lines keep `$$` and the trailing backslash. No evidence quote contains the pipe character. Three source lines that hold a pipe were replaced by a neighbour line: burst-test.sh:290 (the curl call; the comment at line 284 is quoted), burst-test.sh:234 (the regular expression that limits MAX_TOKENS_BASE and MAX_TOKENS_JITTER to 0 or 1 to 9 digits without a leading zero; the error message at line 235 is quoted), build-all.sh:103 (the sed call that turns '/' into '-'; not quoted).
